# Aliens Eye — complete documentation

This file concatenates everything an LLM needs to understand, use, or develop
Aliens Eye. The concise index is `llms.txt`.

---

## What it is

Aliens Eye is an AI-OSINT username scanner (PyPI `aliens-eye`, v2.12.0, MIT
license, Python >= 3.10). It checks whether a username exists across 7,700+
platforms asynchronously — 7,710 enabled sites in the default extended catalog,
or the ~788-site original "standard" catalog via `--catalog standard`.

Highlights:

- ML + heuristic detection over a 30-dimensional feature vector instead of
  naive status-code checks
- Tri-state verdicts (Found / Maybe / Not Found) with confidence percentages
- Profile extraction: display name, bio, avatar (OpenGraph / JSON-LD / per-site CSS)
- Cross-site correlation (`--correlate`): clusters profiles that look like the
  same person by avatar hash, bio, shared links, name
- Recursive expansion (`--recurse-depth N`): follows linked usernames out of bios
- Domain check (`--domains`): is `<username>.{com,io,net,...}` registered/live
- Watch mode (`--watch 6h --notify <url>`): re-scan on an interval, webhook alerts
- Resumable scans (`--resume file.jsonl`)
- Rich terminal UI plus optional interactive browser (`aliens_eye tui`)
- MCP server (`aliens_eye serve`) exposing scanning to LLM agents
- Proxy and Tor support (`--proxy`, `--tor`)
- Site filtering: `--site`, `--exclude-site`, `--no-nsfw`, drop-in `sites.d/` maps
- Control check: every Found is verified by asking the same site for a username
  that cannot exist; identical pages downgrade the hit to Maybe
- Calibrated self-check: per-site precision / recall / F1 / FPR
- Frozen response corpora for reproducible evaluation (`corpus record`,
  `selfcheck --corpus`), ablations with bootstrap confidence intervals
  (`eval ablate`)
- Reports: JSON, CSV, HTML, Markdown, PDF, GEXF, Mermaid, Maltego CSV
- Optional Playwright fallback for JavaScript-heavy pages

> Treat Found/Maybe as leads to verify, not as findings or proof of identity.

---

## Install

```bash
pip install aliens-eye
```

Optional extras:

```bash
pip install "aliens-eye[browser]"   # Playwright fallback for hard pages
python -m playwright install chromium

pip install "aliens-eye[train]"     # scikit-learn, for retraining the ML model
pip install "aliens-eye[correlate]" # Pillow, avatar matching in --correlate
pip install "aliens-eye[pdf]"       # reportlab, for --format pdf
pip install "aliens-eye[tui]"       # textual, interactive `tui` browser
pip install "aliens-eye[serve]"     # mcp, the `serve` MCP server
pip install "aliens-eye[laya]"      # laya + torch + transformers, page-text judge
```

Docker:

```bash
docker build -t aliens-eye .
docker run --rm -it aliens-eye username
```

From source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/arxhr007/Aliens_eye.git
cd Aliens_eye
pip install -e .
```

---

## Usage

```bash
aliens_eye                                  # interactive prompts
aliens_eye username                         # single username
aliens_eye username1 username2              # multiple usernames
aliens_eye username -l advanced             # scan-level variations
aliens_eye username --site github,reddit    # specific sites only
aliens_eye username --no-nsfw               # skip NSFW sites
aliens_eye username --tor                   # route through Tor
aliens_eye username --proxy socks5://127.0.0.1:1080
aliens_eye username --format all --output results
aliens_eye username --no-ml                 # heuristics only
aliens_eye username --profile quick         # quick / full / aggressive presets
aliens_eye username --plain                 # no colors/progress, for CI
aliens_eye username --json-stdout | jq ...  # one JSON line per username
aliens_eye username --json-stdout --only-found
aliens_eye -r results/username_advanced_20260611_120000.json  # view a saved scan
aliens_eye username --correlate --domains
aliens_eye username --recurse-depth 1
aliens_eye username --correlate --format gexf,mermaid,maltego
aliens_eye username --format pdf
aliens_eye username --watch 6h --notify https://hooks.example/aliens
aliens_eye username --resume scan.jsonl
aliens_eye diff results/old.json results/new.json
aliens_eye selfcheck --negatives 2 --report json
aliens_eye corpus record --out corpus/v1 --split all --negatives 4
aliens_eye corpus stats corpus/v1
aliens_eye selfcheck --split holdout --corpus corpus/v1 --report json
aliens_eye eval ablate --corpus corpus/v1 --split holdout
aliens_eye label results/username_basic_20260611_120000.json --out labeled.csv
aliens_eye tui username
aliens_eye serve
```

Custom platforms: drop `{ "site_name": "https://site/{}" }` JSON into
`./sites.d/` (or the user config dir's `sites.d/`); `--sites-dir DIR` adds
another location.

---

## How detection works

HTML detection uses a 30-dimensional feature vector: HTTP status buckets,
username placement (path/title/meta/canonical), error and profile keywords,
DOM structure (images, forms, profile/error CSS classes), structured-data
signals (og:type, JSON-LD Person), response timing, redirect counts, and — in
the legacy scan path — per-site fingerprint matches learned from previous scans.

Two judges vote:

1. Heuristic engine — weighted scoring over the features
2. ML model — logistic regression trained on labeled scans of real and fake
   accounts, shipped with the package, running in pure Python (no sklearn at
   runtime)

The blended probability maps to Found / Maybe / Not Found with confidence. The
loaded model supplies the blend weight and thresholds — the shipped model uses
roughly `0.9 * ml + 0.1 * heuristic`, Found above ~0.62, Not Found below ~0.36.
A missing or invalid model falls back silently to heuristics with the defaults
in `core/detector.py` (0.4 weight, 0.6 / 0.35 thresholds).

A Found must then survive three checks:

- HTTP 404/410 reports as Not Found; other error codes cap at Maybe
- bot-check/error pages cap at Maybe
- the site is asked for a random control username; an identical response caps
  the hit at Maybe (`--no-control-check` skips this, costing one extra request
  per Found)

Catalog sites (maigret/sherlock-derived rules) additionally verify by
presence/absence markers, error codes, `check_type`, custom headers/encodings,
probe URLs, and handle-key matching on JSON API answers.

---

## The laya page-text judge (optional)

An optional third opinion on what a page *shows*, powered by the `laya`
typed-decision engine (`pip install "aliens-eye[laya]"` — pulls torch,
transformers, and a Hugging Face checkpoint; never a hard dependency).

- `--laya` enables it; `--laya-model` picks the checkpoint
  (default `convaiinnovations/laya-multilingual`)
- `--laya-head path/to/head.json` replaces the zero-shot judge with a logistic
  head trained over the encoder's embeddings
- The judge runs on Found/Maybe candidates only: P(profile) at or below the
  veto threshold (0.15) demotes a Found to Maybe; at or above the promote
  threshold (0.90) lifts a Maybe to Found, which then faces the control check
  like any other Found. It never runs on JSON answers or bot-walled pages.
- Verdicts are recorded per-site under `checks["laya"]` and explanation reasons
  `laya_veto` / `laya_promote`.

Measured on the frozen holdout corpus (696 rows): the zero-shot judge does not
beat the shipped detector. The trained head makes it a precision-biased second
opinion — roughly break-even on F1, slightly better precision and false-positive
rate — so it stays opt-in. Train and evaluate it offline:

```bash
pip install "aliens-eye[laya]" "aliens-eye[train]"
python scripts/train_laya_head.py --corpus paper/corpus/v3 --out models/laya_head.json
python scripts/eval_laya.py --corpus paper/corpus/v3 --split holdout --laya-head models/laya_head.json
```

`eval_laya.py` scores four configurations over the same frozen rows —
status_only, shipped, laya_alone, shipped+laya — with bootstrap confidence
intervals and paired delta tests, mirroring `eval ablate`.

---

## Retraining the shipped model

```bash
pip install "aliens-eye[train]"

# 1. scan ground-truth accounts + random negatives (train split only)
aliens_eye train collect --out dataset.csv --negatives 4

# 2. fit and export
aliens_eye train fit --data dataset.csv --out model.json

# 3. score on platforms it never trained on
aliens_eye selfcheck --split holdout --model model.json --report json

# 4. use it
aliens_eye username --model model.json
```

Ground truth: 286 train and 142 holdout site entries. New collection protects
holdout host groups and records `site`, `site_group`, `label_source`, `split`
alongside features. `--split train` scoring measures fit, not generalization.
Training uses grouped folds, nested out-of-fold calibration, and `--max-fpr`
constrained thresholds. Compare candidate precision AND recall on the holdout
before replacing the shipped model — never promote on CV scores.

Offline (no network), reusing a captured corpus:

```bash
aliens_eye train collect --corpus corpus --out grouped-dataset.csv
aliens_eye train fit --data grouped-dataset.csv --out candidate-model.json --max-fpr 0.02
```

`scripts/train_expanded.py` builds labeled pages from expanded-catalog sites in
prepare/record/collect/fit/compare stages under one `--work` directory.

---

## Library API

The package root `aliens_eye` is the stable surface:

```python
import asyncio
from aliens_eye import scan, correlate

report = asyncio.run(scan("torvalds", level="basic"))
# same shape as the CLI's JSON report; pass straight to correlate()
```

Exported names: `scan`, `correlate`, `load_sites`, `match_profile_url`,
`fetch_page` (see `aliens_eye/api.py` docstrings for exact signatures).
`scan(...)` accepts `use_laya` / `laya_model` / `laya_head` among other scan
options. Everything outside the package root is internal.

---

## Repository layout

```
src/aliens_eye/
  cli.py            CLI entry point, argument parsing, run_scan
  api.py            stable library surface
  core/
    scanner.py      async scan orchestration (queue + workers)
    http.py         fetch: retries, backoff, per-domain rate limits
    analyzer.py     HTML feature extraction (selectolax)
    features.py     the 30-dim FEATURE_SCHEMA
    detector.py     heuristic judge + blend + tri-state mapping
    control.py      control-username check
    sites.py        SiteCatalog / SiteDefinition, training groups
    site_rules.py   catalog-rule verification scan path
    laya_judge.py   optional laya text judge + trained-head inference
    netguard.py     SSRF protection
    config.py       ScannerConfig dataclass
    explain.py      per-result explanations
  ml/
    collect.py      dataset collection (train split only)
    train.py        sklearn training, grouped CV, OOF calibration
    inference.py    pure-python logistic regression (runtime)
  corpus/           record/replay of frozen response corpora
  eval/ablate.py    detector-config comparison with bootstrap CIs
  data/             sites.json, extended_sites.json, model.json, ground truth
scripts/
  train_expanded.py   expanded-catalog training pipeline
  train_laya_head.py  train the laya embedding head offline
  eval_laya.py        evaluate laya configurations against a frozen corpus
  verify_catalog.py   catalog verification pipeline
tests/                pytest suite; fake fetchers/local aiohttp, no live scans
paper/                captured evaluation corpora + ablation bundles
```

---

## Development workflow

```bash
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m ruff check src tests aliens_eye.py   # lint
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest -q                            # tests
uv build --offline --out-dir <tempdir>                           # package build
python -m twine check <tempdir>/*                                # packaging verify
python aliens_eye.py sites stats --catalog extended              # offline catalog inspect
python aliens_eye.py sites validate --catalog extended
```

- Scanner/monitoring tests use fake fetchers or local aiohttp servers; no live
  scans or real webhook delivery needed.
- Validation build artifacts go in a fresh temporary directory, not `dist/`.
- Evaluation rule: candidates must beat the shipped model on holdout precision
  AND recall; training/CV scores alone are never evidence.
